headline: Post-training theory identifies response-coverage collapse and a reference-reset remedy
summary: A 141-page theory paper studies policy optimization for language-model post-training. It constructs a contextual-bandit setting where exact-gradient REINFORCE can lose probability mass on optimal responses even while reward rises, yielding exponentially slow convergence despite favorable initial response coverage. The authors introduce Approximate Policy Mirror Descent, which periodically resets the KL reference to the latest policy, and prove coverage-preserving convergence for stylized PPO/GRPO variants and squared-loss methods including Kimi-style objectives under stated assumptions. The main end-to-end guarantees rely on contextual-bandit and softmax-linear policies over frozen features; the paper does not show that deployed nonlinear LLM training runs exhibit the predicted collapse or gains.
